transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-25
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood CSE), Sofia Patel (Redwood Optimize), Dr. Priya Rao (Cedarbridge Head of ML), Evan Cole (Platform), Marta Ruiz (Security), Liam O'Connor (Product)

Summary (auto): quick pass on pilot metrics, one regression found in QA set, guardrail false positives tuning, next steps: latency sweep, share benchmark, schedule private deployment deep-dive.

Topics: pilot scorecard, prompt set drift, guardrail tuning, quantization impact, private deployment security questions, rollout and rollback playbook.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 40 minutes on the calendar. Quick round robin, then we'll jump into the scorecard.
[00:34] Dr. Priya Rao: Hey thanks, Priya here. Quick note, Evan's got a call at 15:30 so he may drop early.
[01:10] Maya Singh: Cool, we'll keep the sec bits for the middle. Jorge and I looked at the runbook you uploaded — thanks for that.
[01:40] Evan Cole: Yeah minor heads up, we tried the test harness overnight and saw a bunch of p95 latency spikes on longer prompts. Might be related to contextual window growth.
[02:05] Alex Kim: Noted, Maya are those the same prompt buckets we saw last week or new ones?
[02:22] Maya Singh: They're the longer triage prompts, so longer than typical; they push KV cache usage. We ran the baseline on the hosted model and a quantized variant. The hosted baseline p95 was ~380ms for the short set, but went up to 1.2s on the long set for token windows above 1k.
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: Were those tests hitting the same server region? Our users are mostly east coast, we ran on west.
[03:34] Maya Singh: West region — good call. We'll rerun east. Region routing can change p95 by ~30-40ms normally. But the big delta seems sequence-length related.
[04:05] Dr. Priya Rao: The bigger concern is quality. We did an evaluation yesterday on the holdout set. Overall F1 improved vs our in-house model, but we have a cluster of false positives on clinical note normalization — it's skewing the rollback threshold.
[04:40] Sofia Patel: Can you give an example? Is this hallucination or label mismatch?
[04:52] Dr. Priya Rao: Example: prompts with shorthand e.g., 'pt denies CP' were expanded incorrectly in 3/47 cases, plus a couple mis-attributed meds. Possibly guardrail parsing not handling abbreviations.
[05:30] Jorge Alvarez: Hmm that sounds like prompt pre-processing gap more than core model hallucination. Are you tokenizing clinical abbreviations before send?
[05:50] Evan Cole: We do minimal normalization today to avoid changing user text; maybe we need a light canonicalization step.
[06:10] Maya Singh: Ok that's a quick win — a canonicalization layer pre-request plus a small guardrail pattern to catch meds expansion errors should drop FP. We'll add to the prompt set as normalized and non-normalized variants for testing.
[06:40] [crosstalk] Marta Ruiz: Also security question — if we do canonicalization in-platform, does that affect data residency? We need to confirm retention and logging.
[06:58] Alex Kim: Right — Redwood can opt-in/out of retaining raw prompts; for Private deployments it's customer-controlled. We'll follow up with the SOC2 and retention docs.
[07:25] Dr. Priya Rao: Back to scoring: the pilot scorecard shows 87% pass on daily acceptance, but that dips to 73% on complex cases. Our internal bar for rolling to prod is 90% across the full stratified set.
[07:55] Sofia Patel: For the complex tier, we saw some model variant diffs — smaller quantized LLMs produced more conservative outputs (fewer hallucinations) but at higher false negative rates. It's the classic precision-recall tradeoff.
[08:30] Liam O'Connor: So what's the recommended rollback threshold? If we hit more than X false positives we roll back?
[08:50] Maya Singh: We usually recommend a two-metric gate: (1) FP rate < 5% absolute on clinical labels AND (2) aggregate F1 >= 88% over the full stratified test. But it's configurable.
[09:20] Dr. Priya Rao: We need to tune for lower FP even at cost of some recall. False positives meaning incorrectly classifying normal text as an adverse event is unacceptable.
[09:40] Alex Kim: Makes sense. We can run a prompt ensemble where we bias toward conservative decoding and a reranker that prefers higher precision. That will increase cost slightly but reduce FP.
[10:10] [00:10 clip noise] Evan Cole: Quick infra Q — if we enable reranking as an extra RPC call, how much latency additive are we looking at?
[10:30] Maya Singh: Reranker as a lightweight ensemble model usually adds ~45-80ms on our hosted infra, depending on batching. For private dedicated pools the delta is lower because of caching.
[11:05] Dr. Priya Rao: Any data on token-level cost? If we add rerankers and conservative decoding what's the percent cost increase?
[11:25] Sofia Patel: Ballpark: conservative decoding alone (higher top-p temperature tweaks) is minimal token-cost delta. Reranking adds model-inference cost — in our benchmark sheet, a single reranker pass increased unit cost by ~12-18% on average. We'll attach the per-model CSV.
[11:55] Alex Kim: We'll share updated benchmark sheet after Maya's latency sweep. Link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/CB-2027-09 (note: placeholder link).
[12:10] [12:10] Evan Cole: Marta has a list of security Qs — Marta?
[12:20] Marta Ruiz: Yep, main asks: KMS integration details for Private deploy, whether HSM-backed keys are supported, audit log retention granularity, ability to disable token retention, and SAML SSO mapping for RBAC. Also need the pen-test report if available.
[12:50] Alex Kim: We can provide SOC2 report and pen-test summary under an NDA, HSM-backed KMS is supported for Private via customer HSM or KMS bring-your-own-key. Audit logs can be set to 90, 365 days retention options on the console. We'll follow-up on specifics.
[13:25] Maya Singh: For technical items, quick note on quantization — the low-bit 4/4+ quant profiles we tested showed 1.7x throughput improvement but increased LM bias on clinical abbreviations. That may explain the FP cluster.
[13:55] Dr. Priya Rao: Interesting — so quantization can magnify rare tokenization edge cases. We need to ensure the quant profile preserves subword fidelity for clinical tokens.
[14:20] Sofia Patel: We can run a tokenization fidelity check across your vocab of special clinical tokens. If we find collisions we'll recommend a different quant profile or a small vocab patch.
[14:45] Liam O'Connor: How invasive is a vocab patch? That sounds risky for model versioning.
[14:58] Maya Singh: It's a micro-change at tokenization step; we create a pinned model variant with the new vocab and test back-compat. It's a common pattern.
[15:25] [15:25] Jorge Alvarez: On routing/fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is down we can route to a cheaper compatible variant with canary tokens appended; Redwood supports automatic fallback with compatibility mapping. That will help uptime during bursts.
[15:55] Evan Cole: Good. For pilot we want to simulate a failover event and measure user-facing error rate. Can Redwood run an injected-failure test?
[16:10] Alex Kim: Yes, we can simulate capacity constraints and failover; we'll share a runbook.
[16:30] Dr. Priya Rao: Back to the regression we found: is that something we can automatically detect in the eval pipeline?
[16:45] Sofia Patel: Yes, we recommend a guardrail rule that flags token expansions with low pattern match confidence; plus a regression alert when FP delta > 3% week-over-week on the stratified complex tier.
[17:05] [17:05] Marta Ruiz: Also need to confirm that any flagged prompts do not include PHI in logs stored by Redwood — we need a way to scrub or hash identifiers at ingest.
[17:30] Maya Singh: For hosted we can do redaction; for Private you control the deletion and scrubbing policies. We can add a pre-ingest redaction hook to your agent.
[17:55] Dr. Priya Rao: For the holdout eval, could you run an ablation: quantized vs non-quant vs reranker+conservative decoding? We want to see precision-recall curves.
[18:15] Maya Singh: Yep. We'll run ablation and include ROC/PR curves and a CSV with per-case classifications. Expect results by 9/29.
[18:35] Liam O'Connor: On rollout strategy, we prefer a staged rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated metric gates. Is that supported?
[18:55] Alex Kim: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts with metric gates. We can enforce rollback automatically if the guardrail thresholds breach.
[19:20] Maya Singh: Note: gate checks can be per-route or global; we'll set per-clinical-route thresholds for you.
[19:45] Evan Cole: I'll probably have to leave at 15:30, but two quick asks before I go: can you confirm network egress for Private (port lists) and a quick requirements doc for our infra team?
[20:00] Alex Kim: We'll email a one-pager and a VPC peering checklist.
[20:20] [20:20] Jorge Alvarez: Quick demo note — we found one test case where the reranker favored a shorter answer that lost clinical nuance. We should include length penalties in the reranker objective when applying to clinical notes.
[20:50] Sofia Patel: Good catch. We'll add length-aware scoring and threshold on entity preservation.
[21:10] Dr. Priya Rao: Any news on licensing/pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted for pilot scale?
[21:30] Alex Kim: For pilot scale we typically recommend hosted to move faster; Dedicated reserved pools kick in when you need predictable throughput. Pricing-wise pilot runs usually fit into our usage-based tier; we'll include an estimated cost run in the benchmark sheet.
[22:00] Liam O'Connor: If we choose Dedicated, how long to spin up a pool?
[22:15] Maya Singh: Dedicated can be provisioned in 7-10 business days in most regions depending on quota and hardware. Private on-prem is longer.
[22:40] Dr. Priya Rao: On evaluation cadence — we'll keep weekly syncs but shift to bi-weekly after we get the regression fixed.
[23:05] Alex Kim: Sounds good. Let's capture concrete next steps.
[23:25] [23:25] Action recap (auto):
- Redwood to run latency sweep (per-region) and ablation (quant vs non-quant vs reranker) by 2027-09-29 (Maya)
- Cedarbridge to deliver normalized prompt set and guardrail rule examples by 2027-09-28 (Priya / Evan)
- Redwood to share SOC2/pen-test/retention docs and VPC peering checklist by 2027-09-27 (Alex)
- Schedule private deployment deep-dive for week of 2027-10-04 (Alex / Marta)

[24:10] [short silence, some background typing]
[24:30] Marta Ruiz: One last security nuance — is there a way to run a blind eval where we keep PHI in our env and only surface metrics to Redwood?
[24:48] Alex Kim: Yes, we can set up a private metrics-only ingest where only aggregate metrics are sent to Redwood Console; raw traces never leave your VPC. We'll detail that in the follow-up.
[25:15] Maya Singh: Ok final quick note on the false positives — we'll add targeted unit tests to your eval harness that specifically stress abbreviation expansions and med entity mapping. That should surface regressions faster.
[25:40] Dr. Priya Rao: Great. Appreciate the focused plan.
[26:00] Evan Cole: (leaving) Thanks all, will follow up on the peering list.
[26:05] Alex Kim: Thanks Evan.
[27:00] [27:00] Closing: agreed on next steps and deliverables. We'll reconvene next Friday same time unless we move to bi-weekly per Priya's note.
[27:30] [end]

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR errors and occasional mislabeling. References shared: benchmark sheet (link above), guardrail runbook (uploaded to shared folder), VPC peering checklist (to be shared).
file_notes: Pilot is healthcare-genomics adjacent; prioritize tokenization & quantization fidelity checks; unique customer vocabulary list to be onboarded.
